title: A separated local isomorphism injective on generic points is an open immersion
statement: Let $g:Y\to X$ be a separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $Y^0$ be the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y$. Suppose there is an open cover $Y=\bigcup_{i\in I}V_i$ such that every restriction $g|_{V_i}:V_i\to X$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. If for every two distinct $\eta,\eta\prime\in Y^0$ one has $g(\eta)\ne g(\eta\prime)$, then $g$ itself is an open immersion. There is no quasi-compactness or finite-component hypothesis, and $g(Y^0)\subseteq X^0$ is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 09NG, label lemma-characterize-open-immersion, statement and proof; applied in the final paragraph of Tag 09NI.

proof.text: Fix $y,y\prime\in Y$ with $g(y)=g(y\prime)=x$. Choose cover members $V_i,V_j$ containing them. By [def-weil-open-immersion] their images $U_i,U_j$ are open and the chart maps identify $V_i,V_j$ with these open subschemes. Put $W=U_i\cap U_j$, so $x\in W$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] choose an irreducible component $C$ of $X$ containing $x$, and by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] let $\xi$ be its generic point. Thus $\xi\leadsto x$, meaning $x\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$. Every open containing $x$ contains $\xi$ (otherwise its closed complement would contain both $\xi$ and its closure). Hence $\xi\in W$. The inverse homeomorphisms of the two charts give points $\eta_i\in V_i$ and $\eta_j\in V_j$ mapping to $\xi$, with $\eta_i\leadsto y$ and $\eta_j\leadsto y\prime$.

source.place: Tag 09NG, lemma-characterize-open-immersion, first three sentences; component existence is Topology Tag 004W (3)-(4), sobriety is Schemes Tag 01IS

proof.text: We verify that either lifted point $\eta=\eta_i$ or $\eta_j$ belongs to $Y^0$, without assuming $X$ irreducible. Choose an irreducible component $D$ of $Y$ containing $\eta$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and its generic point $\zeta$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Since $\zeta\leadsto\eta$, the corresponding chart $V$ contains $\zeta$. Continuity gives $g(\zeta)\leadsto\xi$, so $C=\overline{\{\xi\}}\subseteq\overline{\{g(\zeta)\}}$. A singleton closure is irreducible: if covered by two closed subsets, the subset containing the point contains its closure. Maximality of the irreducible component $C$ therefore gives $\overline{\{g(\zeta)\}}=C$. The uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober] implies $g(\zeta)=\xi$. Injectivity of the chart homeomorphism then gives $\zeta=\eta$, proving that $\eta$ is generic in $D$.

source.place: Tag 09NG, lemma-characterize-open-immersion, sentence “Note that ...” expanded using maximality of components and Tag 01IS

proof.text: Both $\eta_i,\eta_j\in Y^0$ map to $\xi$, so the assumed injectivity on $Y^0$ gives $\eta_i=\eta_j=: \eta$. In particular $\eta\in V_i\cap V_j$. We will use separatedness only to propagate this coincidence from $\xi$ to its specialization $x$, as an equality of points, without asserting that a topologically dense agreement locus determines morphisms on a nonreduced scheme.

source.place: Tag 09NG, lemma-characterize-open-immersion, assumption (3) identifies the two lifted generic points

proof.text: Let $P=V_i\times_X V_j$. The chart isomorphisms identify $P$ with the open subscheme $W$: maps $T\to V_i$ and $T\to V_j$ with equal composites to $X$ are precisely one map $T\to X$ factoring through both opens, hence through $W$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Pull back the closed diagonal $\Delta_g:Y\to Y\times_XY$ along the map $P\to Y\times_XY$ induced by the inclusions. Its pullback is $V_i\cap V_j\to P$: indeed its test morphisms consist of maps $a:T\to V_i$, $b:T\to V_j$ whose composites to $Y$ are the same map $h:T\to Y$; exactly such an $h$ factors uniquely through the intersection of the two open subschemes. These descriptions give the two inverse maps by the fibre-product universal property. Separatedness gives that $\Delta_g$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] gives that this pullback is a closed immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] its image $E=g(V_i\cap V_j)$ is closed in $W$. It contains $\xi=g(\eta)$, so it contains $x$, since $\xi\leadsto x$ also in the open subspace $W$.

source.place: Tag 09NG, lemma-characterize-open-immersion, penultimate sentence, with the closed-diagonal argument written out; Schemes Tag 01JY and definition Tag 01KK

proof.text: Choose $z\in V_i\cap V_j$ with $g(z)=x$, which exists because $x\in E$. The two chart maps are injective, so $z=y$ in $V_i$ and $z=y\prime$ in $V_j$. Thus $y=y\prime$, proving injectivity of $g$ on all points. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source]: the given cover supplies its source open immersions and the required open-immersion composites. It follows that $g$ is an open immersion. If $Y$ is empty, injectivity is vacuous and the same criterion applies.

source.place: Tag 09NG, lemma-characterize-open-immersion, last two sentences; final source-local criterion is Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.of_forall_source_exists

The item matches it hypothesis by hypothesis (separated, open cover by open-immersion charts, injectivity on Y^0) with the conclusion unweakened. Its stmt_deps are complete. The parent lem-trf-affine-source-stalk-isomorphism-neighbourhood applies it with matching hypotheses. The delivery has no new nodes and no SGA citations, and all 9 cited nodes are Mathlib leaves whose statements I read, so there is no route or tool_use question. Step 1 lifts the generic point ξ of a component through x into both charts. Step 2 shows the lifts lie in Y^0 by maximality of C and sober uniqueness. Step 3 identifies η_i=η_j by hypothesis (3). Step 4 base-changes the closed diagonal of g along V_i×_X V_j≅W; I checked both identifications on T-points, and the diagonal base is X. This makes g(V_i∩V_j) closed in W, so it contains x. Step 5 gives injectivity from the charts and applies the local-source leaf, which I checked against Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.of_forall_source_exists, OpenImmersion.lean:87-95. The fact that a morphism factors through an open subscheme exactly when its image lies in it is used without a node; I accept it as a one-line consequence of def-weil-open-immersion (no Stacks 01IN node exists). proof_deps equals the union of the uses. The only DAG hits for 09NG are the item and its parent, so it is not a duplicate. Edge cases: empty Y, Y=A^1⊔A^1 (hypothesis fails), the doubled-origin line (fails exactly at step 4 without separatedness), non-reduced X, infinitely many components.
